display_contract.back: translations, definitions, grammar/register notes, examples, metadata, and all eight learning layers

source_lesson.title: Good Morning, How Are You All?

cards.title: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر
cards.definition_en: A greeting used in the morning.

layers.concept_expansion: It is a time-specific greeting used in the morning and works in both polite everyday and formal contexts.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ. كَيْفَ حَالُكُمْ؟ — Good morning. How are you all?
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not use it as the ordinary evening greeting; مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر is used later in the day.
layers.connections_and_memory: صباح = morning; خير carries the sense of goodness/well-being.
layers.transfer_prompt: You enter a classroom in the morning. Give the appropriate Arabic greeting before asking how everyone is.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize the phrase in audio and produce it automatically in a morning context.

cards.title: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر
cards.definition_ar: تَحِيَّةٌ تُقالُ في المَساءِ أَو بَعْدَ الصَّباحِ.
cards.definition_en: A greeting used in the afternoon or evening.

layers.concept_expansion: It is the later-day counterpart to صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ. كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ — Good evening. How are you?
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: It is time-sensitive; a neutral greeting such as مَرْحَبًا is safer when time of day is irrelevant.
layers.connections_and_memory: Pair it with صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر as a morning/evening contrast.
layers.transfer_prompt: Choose between صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر and مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر for a 7 p.m. encounter.
layers.mastery_evidence: Select and produce the correct time-of-day greeting without translating word by word.

cards.title: كَيْفَ حَالُكُمَا؟ / كَيْفَ حَالُكُمْ؟

translations.en: How are you two? / How are you all?
translations.ur: آپ دونوں کیسے ہیں؟ / آپ سب کیسے ہیں؟
translations.fr: Comment allez-vous tous les deux ? / Comment allez-vous tous ?

cards.definition_ar: كَيْفَ حَالُكُمَا؟ لِمُخاطَبَيْنِ، وكَيْفَ حَالُكُمْ؟ لِجَماعَةٍ.
cards.definition_en: Use كيف حالكما for exactly two addressees and كيف حالكم for a group.
cards.example_ar: كَيْفَ حَالُكُمَا يا أَحْمَدُ وَمَرْيَمُ؟ كَيْفَ حَالُكُمْ يا أَصْدِقَاءُ؟
cards.example_en: How are you two, Ahmad and Maryam? How are you all, friends?

layers.direct_answer: كَيْفَ حَالُكُمَا؟ addresses two people; كَيْفَ حَالُكُمْ؟ addresses a group.
layers.concept_expansion: Arabic marks number in second-person address: singular forms learned earlier contrast with the dual suffix ـكُمَا and plural ـكُمْ.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: Two neighbors: كَيْفَ حَالُكُمَا؟ A room of classmates: كَيْفَ حَالُكُمْ؟
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not use ـكما merely because a group contains men and women; it specifically means two addressees.
layers.connections_and_memory: The progression is ـكَ / ـكِ for one person, ـكُمَا for two, and ـكُمْ for a group in this A1 contrast.
layers.transfer_prompt: Ask one man, one woman, two people, and then a group how they are, changing the suffix correctly each time.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce all four learned ‘How are you?’ forms and choose them based on gender/number without prompting.

layers.concept_expansion: It is the independent first-person plural pronoun used when the speaker refers to themself together with others.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not confuse نَحْنُ ‘we’ with أَنْتُمْ ‘you all,’ which refers to the listeners rather than the speakers.
layers.transfer_prompt: Change أَنا بِخَيْر to ‘We are fine.’
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize and use نَحْنُ naturally as the first-person plural subject.

cards.title: نَحْنُ بِخَيْر
cards.definition_ar: جُمْلَةٌ تُفيدُ أَنَّ المُتَكَلِّمِينَ في حالٍ جَيِّدَةٍ.
cards.definition_en: A phrase saying that the speakers are doing well.
cards.example_en: How are you two? We are fine, thank you.

layers.concept_expansion: It combines the pronoun نَحْنُ ‘we’ with the previously learned بِخَيْر ‘well/fine.’
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: The response changes the speaker perspective: the question may address two or many people, but respondents use نحن when answering together.
layers.connections_and_memory: Build it compositionally from نَحْنُ + بِخَيْر rather than memorizing an unrelated phrase.
layers.transfer_prompt: Two people are asked how they are. Answer together and add شكرًا.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce the phrase smoothly and understand both component words independently.

cards.title: كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِخَيْر
cards.definition_ar: تَعْبيرٌ يَعْني أَنَّ الأُمورَ كُلَّها جَيِّدَةٌ.
cards.definition_en: An expression meaning that everything is okay or going well.

layers.direct_answer: كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِخَيْر means ‘everything is fine.’
layers.concept_expansion: كُلّ means ‘all/every,’ شَيْء means ‘thing,’ and بِخَيْر expresses being well or okay.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: كَيْفَ الأُمورُ؟ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِخَيْر. — How are things? Everything is fine.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: This describes the general state of things, whereas أَنا بِخَيْر or نَحْنُ بِخَيْر describes people directly.
layers.connections_and_memory: Reuses بِخَيْر in a broader sentence rather than only as a personal response.
layers.transfer_prompt: Contrast ‘I am fine,’ ‘we are fine,’ and ‘everything is fine’ in Arabic.
layers.mastery_evidence: Retrieve the full phrase and distinguish its subject/meaning from personal بِخَيْر responses.

cards.title: شُكْرًا
cards.definition_en: A common expression used to show gratitude.

layers.concept_expansion: It is a broadly useful gratitude expression. The lesson also notes شُكْرًا لَكُمْ as a way to thank a group.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِخَيْر، شُكْرًا. — Everything is fine, thank you.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not confuse شُكْرًا with الْحَمْدُ لله: شكرًا directly thanks a person/context, while الحمد لله expresses praise and thanks to God.
layers.connections_and_memory: Root ش-ك-ر is associated with gratitude and thanking.
layers.transfer_prompt: Someone gives you directions. Respond naturally with the Arabic gratitude expression.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize شكرًا instantly and use it appropriately in everyday interaction.
